summary: PASS. git-status.ts is well-designed: getGitStatus() runs 5 read-only git commands in parallel via Promise.all() for minimal latency; CONFLICT_CODES uses a Set for O(1) XY code lookup covering all 7 conflict states; fetchAndGetStatus() correctly silences fetch failures with .catch(). Tests are thorough (14 tests) with engineered merge conflict, isolated origin/clone pairs to prevent test-order sensitivity, ISO 8601 timestamp regex validation, and standalone-no-remote graceful failure. No blocking issues.

comments.note: getGitStatus() runs 5 git sub-commands in parallel via Promise.all() — a strong architectural choice that minimises latency on every status call. The CONFLICT_CODES Set (O(1) lookup) correctly covers all 7 XY codes for unresolved merge/rebase state. The parallel design is correct because all 5 commands are read-only.

fetchAndGetStatus() uses .catch(() => undefined) to silently ignore ALL fetch errors, not just network errors. This is documented behaviour ('best-effort fetch') and is acceptable since fetchRemote only rejects on spawn-level failures. No blocking issue, but future maintainers should be aware that debugging fetch-related bugs may require temporarily removing the catch.

[documentation-forward] getGitStatus() JSDoc documents modifiedFiles as 'total entries reported by git status --porcelain'. The Documentation agent should clarify that this single count includes staged, unstaged, AND untracked files — callers who expect only modified tracked files may be surprised by untracked entries being counted.

The fetchAndGetStatus test using an isolated origin/clone pair (rather than the shared fixture) is a strong pattern that prevents test-order sensitivity. Worth highlighting as a best practice for future test authors in this project.
